title: ASEAN scam prevention is not converting into resolution, recovery, or durable digital trust
source_unit: GSMA ASEAN Consumer Scam Report 2026, covering Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam
geography: Six ASEAN countries; consumer survey estimates reported by the GSM Association

observations.period: 2026 report; previous 12 months; scam exposure and financial recovery

denominator.unit: GSMA consumer survey across Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam; report sample size not available in the accessible indexed release

scammed_previous_twelve_months.unit: percent of surveyed consumers reporting being scammed in the previous 12 months

victims_lost_money.unit: percent of scam victims reporting financial loss

money_losing_victims_recovered_none.unit: percent of money-losing victims recovering none of their losses

money_losing_victims_recovered_all.unit: percent of money-losing victims recovering all losses

mechanism.value: Digital-finance exposure becomes a trust problem when financial loss is not followed by visible recovery; victimization, loss, recovery, and future digital participation are separate stages

observations.method: GSMA-commissioned consumer survey reported in the 2026 ASEAN Consumer Scam Report; figures are descriptive survey estimates across six Southeast Asian markets.
observations.uncertainty: The accessible official release is an industry-association summary and does not expose the full questionnaire, sample allocation, weights, or administrative validation. Conditional denominators differ across all consumers, victims, and money-losing victims.
observations.subgroup: Consumers in Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam who reported scam experience and financial loss.
observations.counterinterpretation: Self-reported scam and recovery status may omit unrecognized incidents, informal recovery, delayed reimbursement, or cases not reported to the survey; non-recovery does not identify which institution was responsible.

observations.period: 2026 report; reported scam cases and institutional resolution

denominator.unit: Survey respondents reporting a scam and reporting behavior; report sample size not available in accessible indexed release

victims_reporting.unit: percent of scam victims reporting the incident

reported_cases_unresolved.unit: percent of reported scam cases remaining unresolved

channel_trust_effect.value: Consumers with unresolved cases report lower trust in communications channels, digital platforms, and data sharing

mechanism.value: Reporting without visible resolution can weaken the legitimacy of the reporting route itself, creating a recourse deficit beyond the original fraud

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from the GSMA 2026 report summary and GSMA-distributed announcement; the report treats resolution as the outcome of reported scam cases.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary does not define unresolved status, adjudication, time-to-resolution, or whether cases were still open at survey date. Reported-case percentages are not population rates and may reflect selection into reporting.
observations.subgroup: Surveyed scam victims who reported incidents across the six ASEAN markets.
observations.counterinterpretation: Unresolved cases may be complex, recent, cross-border, or awaiting institutional action; lower trust may predate the incident or reflect broader digital insecurity rather than the resolution experience alone.

observations.period: 2026 report; scam channels, worry, and consumer switching

denominator.unit: GSMA consumer survey across six ASEAN markets; channel and switching denominators vary by question

worry_scam_or_hacked.unit: percent of consumers worried about being scammed or hacked

messaging_app_channel.unit: percent of reported scam experiences involving messaging apps

social_media_channel.unit: percent of reported scam experiences involving social media

voice_channel.unit: percent of reported scam experiences involving voice calls

sms_channel.unit: percent of reported scam experiences involving SMS

provider_switching.value: Consumers who experienced scams were more than twice as likely to switch accounts or service providers than consumers who had not been affected

mechanism.value: Scam exposure is changing communication-channel behavior and provider loyalty, making digital trust a consumer-choice and market-exit variable rather than only a security attitude

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from the GSMA 2026 report summary; channel percentages may reflect multi-channel scam experiences and therefore need not sum to 100%.
observations.uncertainty: The public summary does not disclose channel question wording, sampling weights, provider-switching base, or whether switching was completed. Report is industry-commissioned and should not be treated as independent fraud prevalence or market-share data.
observations.subgroup: ASEAN consumers and reported scam victims across Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam.
observations.counterinterpretation: Worry can coexist with continued use, switching can reflect ordinary price or service changes, and channel prevalence may reflect exposure or reporting patterns rather than channel-specific risk.

related_sources.claim: Official GSMA report page and indexed 2026 findings on victimization, unresolved cases, recovery, trust, channels, and switching.
GSMA-distributed announcement describing the report’s unresolved-case, recovery, trust, and digital-participation findings.
Publicly syndicated GSMA announcement used to cross-check the accessible headline figures.

boundary: This record adds an ASEAN digital-consumer trust, scam-harm, resolution, recovery, and switching layer. It does not establish independently verified fraud prevalence, administrative case outcomes, causal trust loss, provider liability, or representative market-level switching.
